info.title: Cursor Cloud Agents API
info.description:
Programmatically create and manage Cursor Cloud Agents that work
autonomously on your repositories. v1 separates a durable agent
from one or more runs: each prompt submission creates a run on the
agent. Streaming and cancellation are scoped to the active run.
Environment endpoints manage the saved environments agents run in.

basicAuth.description:
API key from Cursor Dashboard, supplied as the Basic
Authentication username with an empty password.

bearerAuth.description:
API key from Cursor Dashboard, supplied via
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Equivalent to Basic Auth.

Image.description:
An image input. Provide exactly one of `data` or `url`. When
`data` is provided, `mimeType` is required. When `url` is
provided, Cursor fetches the image and `mimeType` must be
omitted.

data.description: Base64 encoded image bytes (max 15 MB). Mutually exclusive with `url`.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL Cursor fetches. Mutually exclusive with `data`.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the image bytes. Required when `data` is provided; must be omitted when `url` is provided. Supported types are `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, and `image/webp`.

id.description: Explicit model ID returned by GET /v1/models. Omit `model` from the request to use the configured default.

params.description: Per-model parameters such as reasoning effort or max mode. Use only parameters supported by the selected model.

url.description: GitHub repository URL. Required on every repo entry, including when `prUrl` is provided.

startingRef.description: Branch name or commit SHA to use as the starting point. Ignored when `prUrl` is provided.

prUrl.description: GitHub pull request URL. When provided, the agent works on this PR's repository and branches; `startingRef` is ignored. `url` must still be set on the same entry.

type.description: Execution environment type. `cloud` uses Cursor-hosted VMs; `pool` and `machine` route to self-hosted workers.

name.description: Named Cursor-hosted environment, Team Pool, or self-hosted machine name. For `type: pool`, this is the pool name (defaults to `default` when omitted). Unknown pool names return `400`. Omit `repos` with `type: pool` to target a repo-less pool. Name an any-repo pool to send more than one entry in `repos`.

CLIENT_ID.description: OAuth client ID for the MCP server.

CLIENT_SECRET.description: OAuth client secret for the MCP server.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes to request for the MCP server.

name.description: MCP server name exposed to the agent.

type.description: Stdio MCP server. Defaults to `stdio` when `command` is provided.

command.description: Command to start inside the cloud agent VM.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the stdio MCP server inside the VM.

name.description: MCP server name exposed to the agent.

type.description: Remote MCP transport. Defaults to `http` when `url` is provided.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL for the remote MCP server. Userinfo in the URL is not allowed.

headers.description: Headers Cursor sends with every request to the remote MCP server.

name.description: Display name. Auto-derived from the prompt when not supplied at create time. Omitted when no name has been set.

status.description: Agent lifecycle state. Execution status lives on runs.

url.description: URL to view the agent in Cursor Web.

updatedAt.description: When the agent was last updated.

latestRunId.description: ID of the most recent run on this agent, if any.

repos.description: Repository configuration. Empty for no-repo agents.

workOnCurrentBranch.description: When `false` (the default), Cursor pushes commits to a new auto-generated branch. When `true`, commits land on the existing head branch.

autoCreatePR.description: Whether Cursor opens a pull request when the run completes.

skipReviewerRequest.description: Whether to skip requesting the user as a reviewer when Cursor opens a PR.

customSubagents.description: Custom subagents defined at create time. Omitted when none were provided.

repoUrl.description: Repository URL the agent pushed to. Returned without the scheme (for example, `github.com/your-org/your-repo`).

prUrl.description: Pull request URL, when Cursor opened a PR.

RunGit.description:
The agent's current pushed branches and pull requests. This is
per-agent state — every run on the same agent returns the same
`git` snapshot rather than only that run's contributions. Use
the agent's `latestRunId` or the SSE stream to attribute work
to a specific run.

branches.description: Branches the agent has pushed. Stacked agents return one entry per branch.

agentId.description: ID of the agent this run belongs to.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the run in milliseconds. Populated once the run reaches a terminal status (`FINISHED`, `ERROR`, `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`).

result.description: Final assistant reply text. Populated once the run terminates.

git.description: The agent's pushed branches and PRs. Populated once the agent has pushed at least one branch. Per-agent state, not per-run.

args.description: Present and true when the tool arguments were too large to include in the stream.

result.description: Present and true when the tool result was too large to include in the stream.

callId.description: Stable identifier for one tool invocation across updates.

name.description: Public tool name, such as `read_file`, `run_terminal_cmd`, or `mcp`.

id.description: Opaque SSE event id passed back via `Last-Event-ID` to resume the stream. Do not parse — the format is implementation-defined.

name.description: Subagent name. Must be unique within `customSubagents` and cannot collide with built-ins (for example, `explore`, `shell`, `debug`, `computerUse`, `cursorGuide`).

description.description: Short summary used by the main agent to decide when to delegate.

prompt.description: System prompt the subagent receives when invoked.

oneOf.description: Use the parent agent's model selection.

text.example: Add a README with setup instructions

images.description: Image inputs. Each entry must provide either `data` (with required `mimeType`) or `url`. Maximum 5 images, 15 MB each.

name.description: Display name for the agent. Auto-derived from the prompt when omitted.

agentId.description: Optional client-supplied agent identifier in `bc-<uuid>` form. Re-POSTing the same `agentId` returns `409 agent_id_conflict` instead of creating a duplicate. Cannot be combined with `envVars`; omit `agentId` so the server mints one when you need session secrets.

repos.description: Repository configuration. Mutually exclusive with a named cloud environment. Omit both `repos` and `env` (or pass `repos: []`) to start a no-repo agent. On self-hosted targets, only a named any-repo pool takes more than one entry. `machine`, the `default` pool, and repo-backed pools take one and return `400` for more.

workOnCurrentBranch.description:
When `false` (the default), Cursor pushes commits to a new
auto-generated branch (`cursor/...`) based on
`repos[0].startingRef` (or the PR base ref when `prUrl`
is set). When `true`, Cursor pushes directly to that
starting ref — for a non-PR create, that's the branch you
passed in `startingRef`; for a `prUrl` create, that's the
PR's head branch.

autoCreatePR.description: Whether Cursor should open a pull request when the run completes.

skipReviewerRequest.description: Whether to skip requesting the user as a reviewer when Cursor opens a PR. Only applies when `autoCreatePR` is true.

envVars.description:
Session-scoped environment variables for the cloud agent.
Values are encrypted at rest, injected into the agent's
shell, and deleted with the agent. Names must be non-empty,
255 bytes or less, and cannot start with `CURSOR_`. Values
must be non-empty and 4096 bytes or less. Cannot be
combined with a client-supplied `agentId`.

Beta: `envVars` is rolling out. If it isn't enabled for
your account yet, the field is silently ignored on create
rather than failing the request — verify the values are
present on a first run before relying on them in
production.

mcpServers.description: Inline MCP server definitions available to the initial run. Remote servers support `headers` or OAuth `auth`; stdio servers run inside the cloud agent VM and can receive `env`. Server names must be unique.

customSubagents.description: Custom subagents the main agent can delegate to. Names must be unique and not collide with built-ins.

mode.description: Initial conversation mode for the agent's first run.

images.description: Image inputs for the follow-up. Each entry must provide either `data` (with required `mimeType`) or `url`. Maximum 5 images, 15 MB each.

mcpServers.description: Inline MCP server definitions for this follow-up run. When provided, these definitions replace any create-time inline MCP servers for this run.

AgentMode.description: Conversation mode. `plan` explores and drafts a plan before coding; `agent` implements changes directly. On follow-up runs, omit to keep the conversation's current mode; set explicitly to switch modes for that run.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results. Omitted (not `null`) when there are no more pages.

items.description: Runs for this agent, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results. Omitted (not `null`) when there are no more pages.

path.description: Artifact path relative to the workspace's `artifacts/` directory.

items.description: Artifacts produced by the agent. Returns at most 100 artifacts.

url.description: Temporary 15-minute presigned S3 URL for downloading the artifact.

totalTokens.description: Sum of the four token counts above.

usageUuid.description: Internal usage identifier for the run. Omitted when the run has no recorded usage yet.

usage.description: Token usage for this run. Runs without recorded usage report zeros across all fields.

totalUsage.description: Token usage summed across the returned runs.

runs.description: Per-run usage, one entry per run (or a single entry when `runId` is set).

EnvironmentRepoFile.description: The file in a repository that an environment reads its configuration from.

url.description: URL of the repository that holds the configuration file.

path.description: Path of the configuration file in the repository.

name.description: Display name. Omitted when the environment has no name.

owner.description: `personal` for an environment that belongs to one user, or `team` for an environment shared with the team.

updatedAt.description: When the environment was last updated.

environmentJson.description: The environment's latest saved configuration, its `environment.json`, as a JSON-encoded string.

versionId.description: ID of the latest saved environment version. Omitted when no version has been saved.

items.description: Environments, most recently updated first. List items omit `environmentJson` and `versionId`.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results. A page can hold fewer items than `limit`, so keep paging until it's absent. Omitted (not `null`) when there are no more pages.

owner.description: `personal` creates an environment for the API key's user, and `team` creates one for the team.

name.description: Display name. It must differ from the names of the owner's other environments; a name the owner already uses returns `409 environment_name_conflict`.

repos.description: Repositories for the environment, or an empty array for an environment without repositories. Cursor must be able to reach each one through your source control integration; otherwise the request returns `400 repository_access`.

environmentJson.description: The environment's `environment.json`, as a JSON-encoded string, using the same schema as a `.cursor/environment.json` file. An invalid configuration returns `400 validation_error`.

UpdateEnvironmentRequest.description: Send `name`, `environmentJson`, or both. A request with both applies them together, so either both change or neither does.

name.description: New display name. It must differ from the names of the owner's other environments; a name the owner already uses returns `409 environment_name_conflict`.

environmentJson.description: Replacement `environment.json`, as a JSON-encoded string, using the same schema as a `.cursor/environment.json` file. It replaces the whole configuration. An invalid configuration returns `400 validation_error`.

EnvironmentBuildId.description: Unique build identifier, in the form `bld-YYYYMMDD-<uuid>`.

type.description: `INSTALL_FAILED` when the `install` command failed, or `TERMINAL_FAILURE` for other failures.

code.description: Machine-readable cause of the failure, when there is one.

environmentId.description: ID of the environment the build belongs to.

status.description: Build status. A skipped build found nothing to rebuild.

trigger.description: What started the build. `RECURRING` for a scheduled build, `CONFIG_CHANGE` after a configuration or secrets change, or `MANUAL` for one started on request.

draft.description: `true` for a draft build. Agents don't start from a draft build until it's activated.

updatedAt.description: When the build was last updated.

completedAt.description: When the build finished. Omitted while it's in progress.

items.description: Up to 10 builds for this environment, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results. Omitted (not `null`) when there are no more pages.

EnvironmentActiveBuild.description: What an agent you start on this environment boots from, one of its builds or Cursor's default image.

EnvironmentActiveBuildFromBuild.description: The agent starts from one of the environment's builds.

EnvironmentActiveBuildFromUniversalImage.description: The agent starts on Cursor's default image.

title.description: The event's summary, as the History tab shows it.

description.description: The event's details, as the History tab shows them.

current.description: `true` for the event that saved the environment's current configuration.

environmentJson.description: The `environment.json` the event saved, as a JSON-encoded string.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results. Omitted (not `null`) when there are no more pages.

apiKeyName.description: Display name of the API key.

createdAt.description: When the API key was created.

userId.description: Numeric Cursor user ID of the API key's owner. Omitted for service-account / team API keys, which aren't tied to a specific user.

userEmail.description: Email of the API key's owner. Omitted for service-account / team API keys.

userFirstName.description: First name of the API key's owner, when populated.

userLastName.description: Last name of the API key's owner, when populated.

params.description: Concrete parameter values that, combined with the parent model `id`, form a valid model selection. May be empty.

isDefault.description: True for the variant Cursor selects when the user picks this model without explicit `params`.

id.description: Pass this value as `model.id` when creating an agent.

aliases.description: Alternate IDs that resolve to the same model.

parameters.description: Per-model parameter definitions, when the model accepts parameters. Use these to populate `model.params`.

items.description: Recommended models. Use `id` (and optionally `params`) when creating an agent.

SecretVersion.description:
One version of a Cloud Agents secret. A name can have several
versions in one environment or team, each for repositories the
others don't cover. Responses never include a secret's value.

id.description:
Opaque version ID. A version keeps its `id` through changes to
its value, type, or repositories. Always present in lists; a
`201` from a `PUT` leaves it out when the new version isn't
readable yet.

type.description:
`runtime_secret` for a Runtime Secret, `environment_variable`
for an Environment Variable, or `build_secret` for a Build
Secret, which only the Docker build gets.

repos.description:
The only repositories that get this version, lowercase and
sorted, with repository URLs reduced to `host/owner/repo`.
Empty when every repository gets it.

createdAt.description:
When the version was created. Always present in lists; a
`201` from a `PUT` leaves it out when the new version isn't
readable yet.

items.description:
Secret versions, sorted by name. A name with versions for
different repositories appears once per version.

nextCursor.description:
Cursor for the next page. Always `null` for now, because the
list isn't paginated yet.

SecretInventoryOwner.description:
Who holds a secret version: `team` for the team the API key works
in, `user` for a user's personal secrets, or `environment` for an
environment's secrets.

user.description:
The user who owns the secrets, for a `user` owner and a personal
environment. Absent for the team and its environments.

email.description: The user's email, or `null` when the user has none on file.

InventorySecretVersion.description:
A secret version with the owner that holds it. Responses never
include a secret's value.

id.description: The version ID its owner's own list shows.

repos.description:
The only repositories that get this version, or empty when every
repository gets it. Every version has it, including other
members' versions in a team admin's list.

items.description:
Secret versions with their owners, not sorted by name. Other
members' versions come after the rest.

nextCursor.description:
Cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page. A page can
hold fewer than `limit` items, or none, and still have one.

value.description:
The secret's value, 1 to 4,096 bytes of UTF-8 text. No
response or error message includes it.

type.description:
A new version defaults to `runtime_secret`. A change without
`type` keeps the version's type. Build Secrets can't be set
through the API yet.

repos.description:
The only repositories that get this version, such as
`acme/api`, `https://github.com/acme/api.git`, or
`gitlab.com/group/subgroup/project`. An empty array, or
omitting `repos` on a new version, gives it every repository.
A change without `repos` keeps the version's repositories.

id.description: The version's `id`. Pass it as `?id=` to pick this version.

repos.description: The only repositories that get this version.

message.example: NPM_TOKEN has 2 versions, each for different repos. Pass the id of one as ?id= to pick it.

versions.description: Every version of the name, in list order.

CreateSubTokenRequest.description: Provide exactly one active team member identifier.

forUserEmail.description: Active team member email. Case-insensitive. Mutually exclusive with `forUserId`.

forUserId.description: Active team member's numeric Cursor user ID. Mutually exclusive with `forUserEmail`.

accessToken.description: Short-lived access token scoped to the requested user. Pass this to the worker with --auth-token or write it to the file used by --auth-token-file.

expiresAt.description: When the access token expires (1 hour after mint).

userId.description: Numeric ID of the resolved team member.

teamId.description: Numeric ID of the service account's team.

AuthenticationError.description: Body of a `401` response when the API key fails authentication.

code.description:
Machine-readable error code. Possible values include
`unauthorized`, `api_key_not_found`, `plan_required`,
`role_forbidden`, `feature_unavailable`,
`integration_not_connected`, `validation_error`,
`missing_body`, `invalid_model`, `invalid_branch_name`,
`repository_required`, `repository_access`,
`pr_resolution_failed`, `artifact_not_found`,
`service_account_required`, `agent_not_found`,
`run_not_found`, `environment_not_found`, `build_not_found`,
`team_admin_required`, `environment_name_conflict`,
`duplicate_json_key`, `agent_busy`, `agent_archived`,
`agent_id_conflict`, `run_not_cancellable`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `usage_limit_exceeded`,
`stream_expired`, `stream_unavailable`,
`invalid_last_event_id`, `client_cancelled`,
`not_implemented`, `upstream_error`, and
`internal_error`.

helpUrl.description: Optional follow-up link. Populated for codes like `integration_not_connected`.

provider.description: Optional provider identifier. Populated for codes like `integration_not_connected`.

environmentId.description: ID of the existing environment with the requested name, when an `environment_name_conflict` error returns it.

BadRequest.description: Validation error or malformed request body.

Unauthorized.description: Invalid, missing, or unsupported API key. When the API key fails authentication, the body has a top-level `code` and `message` instead of an `error` object.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but insufficient permissions, plan required, or feature unavailable.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. Response includes `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers.

post.description:
Create a Cloud Agent and immediately enqueue its initial run.
The response contains both the durable `agent` and the initial
`run`.

201.description: Agent created and initial run enqueued.

get.description: List agents for the authenticated user, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of agents to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from the previous response.

parameters.name: prUrl
parameters.description: Filter agents by GitHub pull request URL.

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description: Whether to include archived agents.

get.description: Retrieve durable metadata for an agent. Execution status lives on runs.

delete.description: Permanently delete an agent. This action is irreversible. Use POST /v1/agents/{id}/archive for reversible removal.

post.description:
Send a follow-up prompt to an existing active agent. The new
run uses the agent's current conversation and workspace state.
Only one run can be active per agent at a time.

get.description: List runs for an agent, newest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from the previous response.

get.description: Retrieve status and timestamps for a specific run.

Stream Server-Sent Events for one run. Event types are
`status`, `assistant`, `thinking`, `tool_call`,
`interaction_update`, `heartbeat`, `result`, `error`, and
`done`.

- `status` carries `{ runId, status }`. It has no `id` line
  and is replayed at the top of every reconnect.
- `result` carries `{ runId, status, text?, durationMs?,
  git? }`; `text` is the final assistant reply, `durationMs`
  the wall-clock duration, and `git` mirrors `Run.git`.
- `interaction_update` carries the richer SDK-shape update
  used by the TypeScript SDK and is emitted alongside the
  simplified events that share the same event id. Use this if
  you want the full SDK stream; otherwise handle the simplified
  events and ignore it.

Reconnect with the `Last-Event-ID` header to resume after a
disconnect; the event ID must belong to the requested run
otherwise the endpoint returns `400 invalid_last_event_id`.
Responses include the `X-Cursor-Stream-Retention-Seconds`
header; after the retention window the endpoint may return
`410 stream_expired`. `tool_call` event data uses the
`RunStreamToolCallData` schema.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume from a previously received event ID for this run.

X-Cursor-Stream-Retention-Seconds.description: Server-side stream retention window in seconds.

post.description:
Cancel the active run for an agent. Cancellation is terminal —
the run transitions to `CANCELLED`. Cancelling a run that is
already terminal or was never active returns
`409 run_not_cancellable`. To continue the conversation,
create a new run on the same agent.

get.description:
Retrieve token usage for an agent, broken down per run.
`totalUsage` sums input, output, and cache token counts across
every run on the agent, and `runs` lists the same breakdown for
each run. Token usage mirrors the `tokenUsage` shape on the team
usage events endpoint.

This endpoint is in early access. When it isn't enabled for the
account it returns `403 feature_unavailable`. An unknown `runId`
returns `404 run_not_found`.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Scope usage to a single run. Omit to return usage for every run on the agent.

post.description: Archive an agent. Archived agents remain readable but cannot accept new runs until unarchived.
Unarchive an agent so it can accept new runs again.

get.description:
List artifacts produced by an agent. Each artifact's `path` is
relative to the workspace's `artifacts/` directory. Pass that
`path` to GET /v1/agents/{id}/artifacts/download to obtain a
presigned download URL.

Retrieve a temporary 15-minute presigned S3 URL for an
artifact. The `path` query parameter must be a relative path
under `artifacts/` returned by GET /v1/agents/{id}/artifacts.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative artifact path under `artifacts/`.

get.description:
List the saved environments the API key can access, most recently
updated first: the user's personal environments and the team's
environments. Team admins don't see members' personal environments
here.

Team admins and service account API keys see every team
environment. Other callers see a team environment only when they
can access all of its repositories. When those checks run out of
time, a response can leave out team environments it hasn't
verified yet, or stop before the end of the list; they show up in
later requests. A service account API key limited to specific
repositories, and user-scoped tokens minted with it, only list
environments that have repositories, all within that limit. Drafts
and deleted environments aren't included.

An environment that changes during a walk moves to the front, so a
later page can leave it out and repeat another. List items omit
`environmentJson` and `versionId`; call GET /v1/environments/{id}
to load an environment's configuration.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of environments to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from the previous response.

post.description: Create a saved environment. The `201` response is the new environment.

503.description: Cursor couldn't reach your source control provider to check a repository (`upstream_error`). Retry after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

get.description: Retrieve a saved environment and its latest saved configuration. An environment that doesn't exist or isn't visible to the API key returns `404 environment_not_found`.

patch.description: Rename an environment, replace its configuration, or both. A request with both fields applies them together, so either both change or neither does. An environment that doesn't exist or isn't visible to the API key returns `404 environment_not_found`.

204.description: Environment updated. The response has no body.

delete.description: Permanently delete a saved environment. This action is irreversible.

get.description: List the changes to an environment, newest first, as its History tab in the dashboard shows them. An environment that doesn't exist or isn't visible to the API key returns `404 environment_not_found`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of events to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from `nextCursor` on the previous response.

get.description: List an environment's builds, newest first, up to 10 per page. An environment that doesn't exist or isn't visible to the API key returns `404 environment_not_found`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from `nextCursor` on the previous response.

get.description: Find out what an agent you start on this environment boots from, one of its builds or Cursor's default image. An environment that doesn't exist or isn't visible to the API key returns `404 environment_not_found`.

Retrieve one of an environment's builds. An environment that doesn't exist or isn't visible to the API key returns `404 environment_not_found`, and a build ID that isn't one of the environment's builds returns `404 build_not_found`.
Retrieve information about the API key being used for authentication.

List an environment's Cloud Agents secrets, one item per version,
sorted by name. No item includes a value. The list isn't paginated
yet, so `nextCursor` is always `null`.

A service account API key can list its team's environments, and
a user API key or user-scoped token its user's personal
environments too. An API key limited to certain repositories can
list only environments whose repositories all sit inside its
limit. Every other environment returns `404 environment_not_found`.

See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#list-environment-secrets.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Environment ID.

403.description:
Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for
your account (`feature_unavailable`), or a `grok_` API key
(`key_not_supported`).

404.description: The environment doesn't exist or your API key can't list its secrets, including an environment outside its repository limit (`environment_not_found`).

get.description:
Returns a recommended set of explicit model IDs you can pass
to the `model.id` field on POST /v1/agents. To use the
configured default model, omit the `model` field from the
request body entirely.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Environment ID.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Secret name, such as `NPM_TOKEN`.

put.description: Create an environment secret, rotate its value, or change its type or repositories. With `?id=`, the request changes that version. Without `?id=`, a name with no version gets one (`201`), a name with one version has it changed in place (`200`), and a name with several versions returns `409 secret_name_ambiguous`. A `PUT` never adds a second version to a name that has one, and an omitted `type` or `repos` keeps the current one. Build Secrets can't be set or changed through the API yet. See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#set-an-environment-secret.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `id` of the version to change.

201.description: The version was created. `id` and `createdAt` are left out when the new version isn't readable yet.

403.description: Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for your account (`feature_unavailable`), a `grok_` API key (`key_not_supported`), or a team that lets only admins change secrets (`team_admin_required`).

404.description: The environment doesn't exist or your API key can't change its secrets, including an environment outside its repository limit (`environment_not_found`), or `?id=` isn't a version of this name here (`secret_not_found`).

409.description: The name has several versions and no `?id=` (`secret_name_ambiguous`, with `versions`), differs from an existing name only in case (`secret_name_conflict`), overlaps another version's repositories (`secret_scope_conflict`), the environment has 1,000 secrets (`secret_limit_reached`), or another request changed the secret at the same moment (`secret_changed`).

delete.description: Delete one version of an environment secret. This action is irreversible. With `?id=`, the request deletes that version. Without `?id=`, a name with one version has it deleted, a name with no version returns `404 secret_not_found`, and a name with several versions returns `409 secret_name_ambiguous` and deletes nothing. `{name}` must match a listed name exactly, letter case included. Every type can be deleted, Build Secrets included. See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#delete-an-environment-secret.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `id` of the version to delete.

403.description: Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for your account (`feature_unavailable`), a `grok_` API key (`key_not_supported`), or a team that lets only admins change secrets (`team_admin_required`).

404.description: The environment doesn't exist or your API key can't change its secrets, including an environment outside its repository limit (`environment_not_found`), or the name or `?id=` isn't a version here (`secret_not_found`).

409.description: The name has several versions and no `?id=` (`secret_name_ambiguous`, with `versions`).

get.description:
List GitHub repositories accessible to the authenticated user
through Cursor's GitHub App installation. This endpoint has
very strict rate limits (1 request per user per minute, 30
per user per hour) and can take tens of seconds to respond
for users with access to many repositories. Cache responses
aggressively and handle this information not being available
gracefully.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Secret name, such as `NPM_TOKEN`.

put.description: Create a secret for the team the API key works in, rotate its value, or change its type or repositories. With `?id=`, the request changes that version. Without `?id=`, a name with no version gets one (`201`), a name with one version has it changed in place (`200`), and a name with several versions returns `409 secret_name_ambiguous`. A `PUT` never adds a second version to a name that has one, and an omitted `type` or `repos` keeps the current one. Build Secrets can't be set or changed through the API yet. See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#set-a-team-secret.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `id` of the version to change, from the team's secrets list.

201.description: The version was created. `id` and `createdAt` are left out when the new version isn't readable yet.

403.description: Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for your account (`feature_unavailable`), a `grok_` API key (`key_not_supported`), an API key limited to certain repositories (`repository_access`), a team that lets only admins change secrets (`team_admin_required`), or an API key that isn't working in a team or whose user isn't a team member (`team_membership_required`).

404.description: `?id=` isn't a version of this name in the team (`secret_not_found`).

409.description: The name has several versions and no `?id=` (`secret_name_ambiguous`, with `versions`), differs from an existing name only in case (`secret_name_conflict`), overlaps another version's repositories (`secret_scope_conflict`), the team has 1,000 secrets (`secret_limit_reached`), or another request changed the secret at the same moment (`secret_changed`).

delete.description: Delete one version of a secret from the team the API key works in. This action is irreversible. With `?id=`, the request deletes that version. Without `?id=`, a name with one version has it deleted, a name with no version returns `404 secret_not_found`, and a name with several versions returns `409 secret_name_ambiguous` and deletes nothing. `{name}` must match a listed name exactly, letter case included. Every type can be deleted, Build Secrets included. See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#delete-a-team-secret.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `id` of the version to delete, from the team's secrets list.

403.description: Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for your account (`feature_unavailable`), a `grok_` API key (`key_not_supported`), an API key limited to certain repositories (`repository_access`), a team that lets only admins change secrets (`team_admin_required`), or an API key that isn't working in a team or whose user isn't a team member (`team_membership_required`).

404.description: The name or `?id=` isn't a version in the team (`secret_not_found`).

409.description: The name has several versions and no `?id=` (`secret_name_ambiguous`, with `versions`).

post.description:
Create a one-hour user-scoped token for a My Machines worker to run as an
active team member. Requires an agent-scoped team service account
API key. User-scoped tokens can't mint other user-scoped tokens.

byUserId.summary: Identify the user by Cursor user ID

get.description:
List the Cloud Agents secrets of the team the API key works in, one
item per version, sorted by name. No item includes a value. The
list isn't paginated yet, so `nextCursor` is always `null`.

Any team member can list, as can the team's service account API
keys. An API key limited to certain repositories gets
`403 repository_access`, because team secrets reach every
repository.

See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#list-team-secrets.

403.description:
Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for
your account (`feature_unavailable`), a `grok_` API key
(`key_not_supported`), an API key limited to certain
repositories (`repository_access`), or an API key that isn't
working in a team or whose user isn't a team member
(`team_membership_required`).

get.description:
List every Cloud Agents secret the API key can list, one item per
version, with the owner that holds it. No item includes a value.

Without `scope` or `environmentId`, the list includes the team's
secrets and the user's personal secrets for an API key with no
repository limit, and the secrets of the environments the key can
list. A team admin using their own user API key without `repo` also
gets the other members' personal secrets and their personal
environments' secrets, with their `repos`.

Keep paging until `nextCursor` is `null`, and send the same filters
with each `cursor`.

See https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints#list-secrets.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
`team` lists only the team's secrets, `user` only the user's
personal secrets, and `environment` only environment secrets.
`members` lists the user's personal secrets and, for an explicit
team admin using their own user API key or session, every other
current member's personal secrets after them, but none of their
personal environments' secrets. For everyone else it returns the
same response or refusal as `user`.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description:
List only this environment's secrets. Combining it with
`scope=team`, `scope=user`, or `scope=members` returns
`400 validation_error`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Only versions with this name, ignoring case.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description:
Only the versions an agent on this repository gets: versions for
that repository and versions for every repository. Combining it
with `scope=members` returns `400 validation_error`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum items per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page.

403.description:
Plan or role not allowed, the environments API isn't enabled for
your account (`feature_unavailable`), or a `grok_` API key
(`key_not_supported`). With `scope=team`, an API key limited to
certain repositories (`repository_access`) or one that isn't
working in a team or whose user isn't a team member
(`team_membership_required`). With `scope=user` or
`scope=members`, an API key limited to certain repositories
(`repository_access`) or one that doesn't act for a user
(`user_required`).

404.description: `environmentId` names an environment that doesn't exist or that your API key can't list (`environment_not_found`).
